newsitem.title: UK: Bulk of LME copper stocks rise came from Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Bulk of LME copper stocks rise came from Singapore.

text.p: The bulk of the 11,475-tonne LME inventory rise in copper on Tuesday was due to metal delivered into the Singapore warehouse, data shows.
Stocks in Singapore increased by a net 9,850 tonnes, with 10,500 tonnes arriving and 650 tonnes delivered out of the warehouse.
Several LME floor traders said they believed the metal delivered was of Chinese origin.
Rotterdam saw an increase of 1,125 tonnes, Helsingborg by 400 tonnes and Bilbao 100 tonnes.

The increase brings the total LME copper inventory to 134,700 tonnes, up slightly from a 6-1/4 year low hit in late November of 90,050 tonnes, but still well below the 275,775 tonnes seen in September.
Prices initially slumped on Tuesday morning when the stocks data was released, but they recovered in ring trading and tested the $2,200 resistance level.
"Location is the all important thing," one floor trader said, adding that the European and the US physical market remained reasonably tight.
"It's unlikely that any of the material in the Far East will find its way into Europe to allievate the tightness," he added.
Rotterdam material was showing a stong premium over LME cash, traders said.
